credits.source: Art in the Mathematics Classroom: Islamic Geometry (ATM conference handout)
credits.creator: Charlotte Webb
credits.note: The sequence of two triangles, the hexagon, and lines through the triangles' crossings carried to the hexagon follows the handout's six-fold construction. The handout repeats the large hexagon; the real tilework repeats the smaller hexagon of step 7 instead.

credits.source: Computer Graphics and Geometric Ornamental Design, chapter 3
credits.creator: Craig S. Kaplan
credits.note: Describes this pattern as six-pointed stars placed in a tiling of hexagons, which confirmed the repeat used here.

given.A: Any point to the right of O. The distance OA is the radius of the first circle, and the unit for every length.

steps.text: Draw a horizontal line, put the compass point on it and draw a circle. Keep the compass at this opening until the end.
Put the compass point where the circle crosses the line on the right and draw a circle through the centre. Do the same on the left. The two new circles touch at the centre.
The two new circles cross the first one at four more points. Draw a circle of the same size around each of them. Six circles now ring the first, and their crossings divide it into six.

The six circles cut the first circle at six points, one every 60°. Join every other point to draw a triangle pointing right, then join the other three to draw a triangle pointing left. The two triangles make a six-pointed star and cross each other at six points.
Join the six points on the circle in order to draw a hexagon with a corner at each end of the horizontal line. It frames the drawing.

Rule a line through every other crossing of the two triangles, six lines in all, and carry each one on until it meets the hexagon at both ends. Where these lines cross near the centre they draw a smaller star whose points are the crossings you started from.

In the finished pattern every small hexagon is shared by three stars, so the tile reaches only to the middle of each one. Find the middle of the right-hand corner hexagon by ruling its diagonal from its top-left corner to its bottom-right corner and marking where it crosses the horizontal. Turn that point round the centre in steps of 60° to get the middles of the other five, and join the six points: this smaller hexagon is the tile that repeats.

ink.text: Go over six small hexagons, one in each corner of the tile: each has a corner of the tile as one of its corners and is cut off by the new lines. Between them the six-pointed star is left in the middle.

pattern.text: Repeat the small tile side to side. Each corner hexagon is completed by the two tiles that share it, so every hexagon touches three stars, and hexagons meet only at their corners, where two star points fit between them.

expect.note: Golden values, in units of OA, computed by the engine and checked for six-fold symmetry, no slivers, and pieces that exactly fill the tile. The hexagons have side 1/3 and the star's points reach 1/√3.
